## Overview

NanoQuRe provides quality control tools for Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT)
sequencing data. Starting from a sequencing summary file produced by an ONT
basecaller (Guppy or Dorado), the package generates interactive plots and
summary tables, and can bundle them into a self-contained HTML report with a
single function call.

## Installation

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("LRB-IIMCB/NanoQuRe")
```

## Input data

NanoQuRe works on the per-read columns of a sequencing summary. The following
columns are required for the complete report:

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `sample_id` | character | Sample identifier (absent from raw summaries) |
| `run_id` | character | Run identifier |
| `channel` | integer | Channel number |
| `start_time` | numeric | Read start time in seconds |
| `duration` | numeric | Read duration in seconds |
| `sequence_length_template` | numeric | Read length in nt |
| `mean_qscore_template` | numeric | Mean Q-score of the read |
| `passes_filtering` | logical | Whether the read passed the basecaller filter |

`generate_report()` accepts either a path to a tab-separated summary file or a
data frame. From a file, only the columns listed above are read. If the file
has no `sample_id` column, the file name (without directory and extension) is
used as the sample identifier, and `passes_filtering` may be stored as a
logical value, as TRUE/FALSE text, or as 1/0.

The individual plotting and table functions take a data frame. In that case
`sample_id` has to be added by the user and `passes_filtering` has to be
logical:

```{r load-real, eval = FALSE}
seq_summary <- vroom::vroom("sequencing_summary.txt", delim = "\t",
                            show_col_types = FALSE)

# raw summaries carry no sample identifier
seq_summary$sample_id <- "my_sample"

# the pass/fail flag may be read as text; the functions expect a logical column
seq_summary$passes_filtering <- as.logical(seq_summary$passes_filtering)
```

The examples below use the dataset bundled with the package (1000 reads from
a single MinION run):

```{r load-data}
library(NanoQuRe)

data(sample_data)
```

## Generating a full QC report

The main entry point is `generate_report()`. It counts the unique `sample_id`
values in the input, selects the single-sample or the multi-sample template
accordingly, and renders a self-contained HTML file.

```{r generate-report, eval = FALSE}
generate_report(sample_data, output_file = "my_QC_report.html")
```

The report is written to `output_dir` (the working directory by default) and
its path is returned. `output_file` is a file name only; a directory is given
through `output_dir`. The `platform` argument (`"minion"`, the default, or
`"promethion"`) selects the flow cell layout of the pore activity heatmap.
Flongle flow cells are not supported.

```{r generate-report-file, eval = FALSE}
# a raw summary file from a PromethION run; the sample is named after the file
generate_report("sequencing_summary_run42.txt",
                output_file = "run42_QC_report.html",
                output_dir = "reports",
                platform = "promethion")
```

## Multi-sample reports

Several data frames or file paths can be passed to `generate_report()`, which
combines them. The multi-sample template is chosen when more than one unique
`sample_id` is present:

```{r multi-sample, eval = FALSE}
generate_report(sample_data_A, sample_data_B, output_file = "multi_QC_report.html")
```

A sample should contain reads from one run. If one `sample_id` spans several
`run_id` values, `generate_report()` warns, because reads from different runs
would share one time axis, and the pore activity heatmap of that sample is
replaced by a notice.

## What the report contains

The report bundles the output of the individual NanoQuRe functions listed
below, each followed by a short caption with values computed from the data.
The [Using Individual Functions](individual-functions.html) vignette covers
each function in detail.

| Function | What it shows |
|---|---|
| `sequencing_stats()` | Run-level summary table |
| `quality_stats()` | Quality metrics table (N50, mean Q-score, longest read) |
| `plot_read_lengths()` | Read length distribution with mean and N50 lines |
| `plot_cumulative_yield()` | Cumulative bases over time, pass and fail reads |
| `plot_quality_distribution()` | Q-score distribution, pass and fail reads |
| `plot_average_speed()` | Translocation speed [nt/s] per hour |
| `plot_seq_throughput()` | Yield per hour |
| `plot_active_channels()` | Channels producing reads in each time window |
| `plot_double()` | Read length and Q-score per hour |
| `pore_activity_heatmap()` | Per-channel yield over time and on the flow cell layout |
